# description:
# In the input you will see a grid containing random shapes formed by colored pixels.
# To make the output grid, mirror the shapes horizontally, leaving a 1-pixel vertical line of the background color in the center.
# Ensure the mirrored shapes maintain their original colors.

def main(input_grid):
    # Plan:
    # 1. Determine the middle column to place the vertical line of the background color.
    # 2. Identify all the objects/shapes in the input grid.
    # 3. Mirror each shape horizontally across the center line.
    # 4. Place the mirrored shapes onto the output grid.

    # Define background color
    background_color = Color.BLACK

    # Calculate the middle of the grid
    width = input_grid.shape[1]
    middle_column = width // 2

    # Initialize the output grid with the background color
    output_grid = np.full(input_grid.shape, background_color)

    # Detect all shapes (non-background objects) in the input grid
    shapes = detect_objects(input_grid, background=background_color, monochromatic=False, connectivity=8)

    # Function to mirror a shape horizontally
    def mirror_shape(shape, center_x):
        mirrored_shape = np.fliplr(shape)
        return mirrored_shape

    for shape in shapes:
        # Get the bounding box of the shape
        x, y, w, h = bounding_box(shape, background=background_color)

        # Crop the shape to get a sprite
        sprite = crop(shape, background=background_color)

        # Mirror the sprite
        mirrored_sprite = mirror_shape(sprite, middle_column)

        # Calculate new position for the mirrored sprite
        new_x = x
        new_y = middle_column + (middle_column - y - w)

        # Blit the original and mirrored sprite onto the output grid
        blit_sprite(output_grid, sprite, x, y, background=background_color)
        blit_sprite(output_grid, mirrored_sprite, new_x, new_y, background=background_color)

    # Place a vertical line of the background color in the center
    output_grid[:, middle_column] = background_color

    return output_grid

    height = np.random.randint(10, 20)

    # Initialize the grid with the background color

        y = np.random.randint(0, width // 2 - shape_width)

        # Random shape color

def main(input_grid):
    # Plan:
    # 1. Detect all the non-black objects in the grid.
    # 2. For each object, mirror it across the vertical central axis.
    # 3. Invert the colors of the mirrored shapes.
    # 4. Place the mirrored and color-inverted shape on the output grid.

    # Detect all colored objects in the input grid
    objects = detect_objects(input_grid, background=Color.BLACK, monochromatic=True, connectivity=4)

    # Create the output grid initialized with the input grid
    output_grid = input_grid.copy()

    # Width of the grid for mirroring calculation
    width = input_grid.shape[1]
    central_axis = width // 2

    for obj in objects:
        # Get the position and color of the object
        x, y = object_position(obj, background=Color.BLACK, anchor="upper left")
        sprite = crop(obj, background=Color.BLACK)
        obj_color = sprite[0, 0]

        # Mirror the object across the central vertical axis
        mirrored_x = 2 * central_axis - x - sprite.shape[1]

        # Invert the color of the mirrored object
        inverted_color = invert_color(obj_color)

        # Blit the mirrored and color-inverted object onto the output grid
        blit_sprite(output_grid, sprite, mirrored_x, y, background=Color.BLACK)
        output_grid[y:y+sprite.shape[0], mirrored_x:mirrored_x+sprite.shape[1]] = inverted_color

    return output_grid

def invert_color(color):
    # Function to invert a color
    # Assuming the colors are represented as integers from 1 to 9 (excluding black which is 0)
    if color == Color.BLACK:
        return Color.BLACK
    all_colors = list(Color.NOT_BLACK)
    return all_colors[len(all_colors) - all_colors.index(color) - 1]

def main(input_grid):

def main(input_grid):

    # 2. Identify all the objects/shapes in the input grid.
    # 3. Mirror each shape horizontally across the center line.
    # 4. Place the mirrored shapes onto the output grid.

    # Define background color
    background_color = Color.BLACK

    # Calculate the middle of the grid
    width = input_grid.shape[1]
    middle_column = width // 2

    # Initialize the output grid with the background color
    output_grid = np.full(input_grid.shape, background_color)

    # Detect all shapes (non-background objects) in the input grid
    shapes = detect_objects(input_grid, background=background_color, monochromatic=False, connectivity=8)

    # Function to mirror a shape horizontally
    def mirror_shape(shape, center_x):
        mirrored_shape = np.fliplr(shape)
        return mirrored_shape

    for shape in shapes:
        # Get the bounding box of the shape
        x, y, w, h = bounding_box(shape, background=background_color)

        # Crop the shape to get a sprite
        sprite = crop(shape, background=background_color)

        # Mirror the sprite
        mirrored_sprite = mirror_shape(sprite, middle_column)

        # Calculate new position for the mirrored sprite
        new_x = x
        new_y = middle_column + (middle_column - y - w)

        # Blit the original and mirrored sprite onto the output grid
        blit_sprite(output_grid, sprite, x, y, background=background_color)
        blit_sprite(output_grid, mirrored_sprite, new_x, new_y, background=background_color)

    # Place a vertical line of the background color in the center
